items.duty_text: Fulfill the requirements of NYC Charter § 1053.
List all candidates in a ranked choice election on the ballot.
Design the ballot to permit voters to rank up to five candidates, or all candidates when fewer than five are on the ballot.
Organize ranked-choice ballot sections as a grid with the required layout, candidate placement, ranking columns, labels, and the word “choice.”
Provide plain-language ballot instructions explaining how to mark the ballot, rank candidates, and any other information deemed necessary by the Board.
Present ballot instructions above or next to the first ranked-choice election on the ballot.
Provide line-drawing illustrations supplementing the ballot instructions.
Include brief instructions within the area for each ranked-choice election.
Design ballots, to the greatest extent practicable, to allow electronic tabulation of rankings and electronic detection of ballot marking so voters can correct equal rankings.
When practicable, group ranked-choice elections together and present them on a separate ballot page or one side of a combined ballot page.
Separate multiple ranked-choice elections on the same ballot page with bold black lines.
Arrange multilingual ballot text, to the extent practicable, so non-English text can be compared with corresponding English text and languages are clearly separated and visually distinct.
Use black font on a white background for instructions, to the extent practicable.
Ensure party-indicating coloring on a primary ballot does not cover ballot instructions, to the extent practicable.
Base the final ballot design on ballot-design-software space and design limitations while following ballot-design best practices to the greatest extent possible.
Assign a code to each geographic school district and create voter registration materials that include these codes.
Upon request by the Department of Education, provide coded voter registration forms to each public or private high school within the city.
